summary:
Small farms make the same rotation decisions as large agribusinesses, but rarely have an agronomist or a data analyst. Crop Compass is a mobile and web app that puts a farmer's own field data next to NASA climate history for that exact location. The farmer marks the field on a map, enters soil observations or lab results, sees what NASA POWER data shows about recent winters and springs there, plans a 1–10 year crop sequence with automatic crop-family warnings, compares two plans, and keeps buyer quotes and budget notes in one place.
It answers the Field Shift challenge by combining NASA Earth observations, local soil information, crop characteristics and the farmer's own plans and costs in one tool. Every number is labelled as farmer-entered, NASA data, an official reference or a stated assumption. It supports decisions rather than predicting outcomes, and it tells the farmer when a question needs an agronomist.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Crop Compass helps a small farmer in Lithuania, Latvia or Estonia plan what to grow on a specific field and keep everything needed for that decision in one place. The app has ten screens:

- Home: current season, field setup status, rotation horizon and shortcuts. Missing data stays visibly missing.

- My farm: pick a country and a point on a full-screen map, search for places, draw a rough field boundary to estimate area, switch between street, satellite and NASA MODIS layers, and enter soil texture, drainage, pH, organic matter and lab-measured ECe.

- Seasons: a seven-day forecast for the field point, with wet-ground and snowmelt cautions based on modelled topsoil moisture, snow depth, temperature and rain. The thresholds are shown in the app.

- Weather and data: NASA POWER daily temperature and corrected precipitation, summarised by year, winter (Dec–Feb) and spring (Mar–May) for the last five complete years at the selected coordinate.

- Rotation: plan 1 to 10 years, choose a crop for each year, and get warnings when a botanical family repeats in consecutive years or returns sooner than the assumed minimum interval (3 years for Brassicaceae, Fabaceae and Solanaceae). Save one plan as Plan B and compare it with Plan A year by year.

- Markets: country-specific links to selling channels and a log of buyer leads and quotes (product, buyer, volume, €/t).

- Budget: income and cost arithmetic using only the farmer's own numbers.

- Crop and salinity guide: compares a lab-measured ECe with indicative FAO AquaCrop salinity thresholds where a cited value exists; a missing reference value is shown as missing, not as zero.

- Seasonal guide and About: field tasks by season and a full explanation of data sources and limitations.

HOW IT WORKS

The app is built in Flutter (Dart), so one codebase runs in a browser, on Android and on iOS. It calls the NASA POWER daily point API (T2M, PRECTOTCORR) for the selected coordinate and aggregates the daily values into annual, winter and spring summaries. Winters are assigned correctly across the year boundary (December of the previous year plus January and February), and NASA fill values are treated as missing. The Open-Meteo forecast API provides the seven-day context. Maps use flutter_map with OpenStreetMap tiles, Esri World Imagery and NASA GIBS MODIS corrected reflectance (bands 7-2-1). Results are cached on the device: forecasts for up to 4 hours, NASA summaries for one day. If a refresh fails, older data is shown with an "offline / last updated" label instead of being presented as fresh. All farmer data stays on the device.

DESIGN PRINCIPLES

- Evidence labels on displayed values: farmer-entered, official reference, gridded model estimate or planning assumption.

- No invented numbers: the app does not forecast yield, profit or demand, and says so.

- Built for small farms: plain language, phone-first layout, useful even with partial data.

- Localised: English, Lithuanian, Latvian and Estonian language resources.

WHY IT MATTERS

Rotation mistakes are expensive and slow to fix, and small farms carry that risk with the least support. Crop Compass gives them the starting point a large farm's analyst would prepare: a field-specific view of climate, soil, rotation risks, buyers and costs. It also makes clear which questions still need local expertise.

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE NEXT

Field-level vegetation monitoring (MODIS and Sentinel-2 NDVI) to show bare-soil periods; longer NASA climate records with frost and drought indicators; a farm history log so planning becomes more personal each season; automatic EU Agri-food price references; and testing with Lithuanian farmers and agronomists.

TOOLS

Flutter and Dart; packages http, shared_preferences, flutter_map, latlong2, url_launcher, geolocator and flutter_localizations; Flutter test framework (unit and widget tests for the NASA POWER summaries and field selection); Android Gradle build; VS Code; Git.
